newsitem.title: JAPAN: GOLF-THIRD STRAIGHT CHUNICHI CROWNS WIN FOR OZAKI.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THIRD STRAIGHT CHUNICHI CROWNS WIN FOR OZAKI.

text.p: Japan's top player Masashi "Jumbo" Ozaki repulsed a strong foreign challenge including world number one Greg Norman on Sunday to win his third straight Chunichi Crowns tournament,
Ozaki, who went into the final round with a one stroke lead, hit a three under par 67 for a 13-under par total of 267.
Ozaki, who has won more tournaments than any other Japanese, had four birdies and a bogey in the final round.
American Brian Watts was runner up two strokes back on 269 after four birdies and two bogeys in his 68.
Norman, who with Watts started the day one stroke behind Ozaki, managed only a par round which included two birdies and two bogeys to finish third at 271.
The win was Ozaki's second in only three appearances on the Japanese tour this season, following a season-opening win at the Token Corp. Cup in March.
"At the (U.S.) Masters, I didn't have a good feel for my shots, but this time, it was different," said Ozaki, who finished a disappointing 42nd last month in Augusta, Georgia.
"I hope this is a good sign before the U.S. Open in June," he said.
Ozaki's win was laced with some controversy as Norman cautioned him on the second hole of the final round about placing his club on the grass behind the ball before swinging.
Tour director Zensuke Okabe, however, dismissed the incident, saying the competition committee had not received any official complaint from the Australian.

"Placing the club behind the ball did not improve the lie of the ball. In Europe and the United States, this is a delicate issue, but on Japan's Korai grass this does not apply, so we want to handle this according to the rules," Okabe said.

Golf courses in Japan feature shorter roughs compared to those in the United States and use "Korai" grass, which usually does not cause the ball's lie to change even if the grass behind the ball is pressed or patted down.
